newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica's Zulu party faces financial woes -- leader.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica's Zulu party faces financial woes -- leader.

text.p: Zulu chief Mangosuthu Buthelezi, leader of South Africa's largest black opposition party, said on Saturday it faced severe financial difficulties ahead of the 1999 national elections.
"We don't have money," he told a news conference at an annual gathering of thousands of supporters of his Zulu-based Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP).
Buthelezi, a longtime rival of South African President Nelson Mandela, said the party had closed three of its 14 national offices.

"Psychologically it is very bad that we should be closing offices when the elections are in the offing. But it seems that even the richer parties like the ANC have this problem too," he said, referring to Mandela's African National Congress.

Senior party member Joe Matthews, deputy safety and security minister in the national government, said the party needed about 92 million rand ($20 million) to fight South Africa's second all-race elections effectively.
"That may be more than we require. We think we have got in the IFP the organisational ability to cut costs," he said.

Inkatha will be competing against its fiercest rival, the ANC, to retain control of its powerbase in KwaZulu-Natal province. The party gained a narrow victory in the province in the first all-race elections in April 1994.
